question: How does available measurement information affect reconstruction?
model_inputs: pressure-only + physics; pressure + velocity probes + physics; dense observations
metrics: regional relative L2 for u v p; first-harmonic diagnostics
decision_notes: Controlled sparse comparison accepted; dense observations are a representational ceiling because that run also skips Adam and uses a longer L-BFGS budget

question: Does increasing cylinder pressure-tap count improve reconstruction?
model_inputs: pressure-only + physics (8 taps); pressure-only + physics (16 taps); pressure-only + physics (32 taps)
metrics: regional relative L2; first-shedding-harmonic relative L2 amplitude ratio correlation and phase
decision_notes: Matched settings verified; only NTaps changes as an input setting; convergence effort is reported but not treated as a controlled parameter; more taps improve selected local fields but do not recover the downstream wake

question: Does wake-biased collocation recover information absent from wall measurements?
model_inputs: uniform collocation; wake-biased random collocation; wake-biased grid collocation
metrics: regional relative L2; first-shedding-harmonic relative L2 amplitude ratio correlation and phase
decision_notes: Only the interior collocation sampling flag differs; effort is not controlled. 5503 L-BFGS evaluations (uniform) against 43676 (wake-biased random) and 37713 (wake-biased grid): a 6.9-7.9x gap that is structural rather than incidental, since the uniform arm is 01_baseline_physics_only and its matched-effort re-run was attempted and discarded 2026-08-28. Evaluation count is not an accuracy proxy, so neither the near-body gain nor downstream loss is assigned causally to sampling. Wake-biased sampling raises far-core amplitude about 16x while correlation falls about 40 percent: amplitude without phase. All three endpoints retain order-one downstream error; no arm recovers the wake

question: Does the trained network improve the Karman prior or reproduce it?
model_inputs: prior only; pressure-only + physics; pressure-only + physics + Karman prior
metrics: prior error; hybrid error; relative improvement; learned-correction magnitude; harmonic diagnostics
decision_notes: Central dissertation comparison accepted; results and final figures in 6_analysis/

question: Does wake-biased collocation improve the prior-assisted reconstruction?
model_inputs: Arm 15 (prior + uniform collocation); Arm 10 (prior + wake-biased grid)
metrics: regional relative L2; harmonic diagnostics; learned contribution relative to the prior
decision_notes: Symmetric flag diff verified: only WakeBiasedGridSampling differs and forward code hashes match. The wake-biased endpoint has less learned near-wake improvement and a larger far-field error than the uniform endpoint. Effort is not controlled (34643 vs 26129 L-BFGS evaluations); evaluation count is not an accuracy proxy so the observed difference is descriptive rather than a causal sampling effect. Far-core v1 is strongly constrained around the analytical prior by the bounded radial-trust ansatz and must not be read as an unconstrained network reconstruction

question: Is the prior-assisted result robust to pressure noise?
model_inputs: Arm 15 (clean); Arm 11 (1 pct); Arm 12 (5 pct); Arm 13 (10 pct)
metrics: regional relative L2; harmonic diagnostics; learned contribution relative to the prior
decision_notes: Manifest reports input_mismatch: LBFGSCheckpointIters is present in Arms 11 and 13 only (read-only accepted-step callback that does not enter the objective). Far-core v1 is strongly anchored by the V1RadialTrust blend and cannot be interpreted as unconstrained learned robustness; noise erodes the learned near-body contribution monotonically in the near wake. Single seed per level and 11x effort spread, so direction only, no dose-response magnitude
